candidates.rationale: The current watcher consumes the entire available tail with readlines(), commits its offset before JSON decoding, and suppresses malformed records. A record split across polls is lost as two invalid fragments. This establishes a local announcement-loss bug; no voice daemon was launched.

Offset advances over all read bytes before decoding; no fragment buffer.

guards: Initial contents are intentionally skipped at startup.
The trigger requires an append split across polling reads; complete newline records work.
last_model suppresses duplicate model announcements but cannot reconstruct a partial record.

candidates.rationale: After startup the offset only advances when size is greater than last_pos; truncation and file identity changes are never handled. A shorter replacement is ignored, and later growth resumes at the stale offset. This is distinct from incomplete-record handling.

source_checks.observation: Tracks a byte offset but neither inode identity nor shrinkage.
The watcher is reachable from --watch with a selected path.

guards: The path must exist; disappearance is skipped without resetting state.
The failure is conditional on truncation/replacement after startup; append-only logs are unaffected.

candidates.rationale: The cached-audio branch interpolates raw text inside AppleScript source passed to osascript -e. Filename sanitization affects only the cache lookup. guards: A matching WAV is required to enter the notification branch.
The playback lock serializes playback; it does not escape AppleScript.
A subprocess argv list avoids shell parsing but osascript still interprets its -e argument as source.

candidates.rationale: spawn_writer_daemon slices an 8192-byte envelope with its public len field before ExergyPacket validation. A service participant supplying len > 8192 causes a Rust bounds panic in the writer thread. The normal publish_exergy_packet helper prevents oversized packets, so malformed direct/alternate IPC publishing is a necessary precondition; IPC access and deployed exposure were not exercised.

source_checks.observation: Received envelope length is used directly in a slice.
Public envelope fields permit representing invalid lengths; normal helper bounds its own messages.
Python-facing start_writer_daemon invokes the affected writer.

guards: The standard publisher rejects packed.len() > 8192.
Worker stop/max_events bound its loop, not envelope length.
No memory-unsafety claim: this is a bounds panic before unpack rejection.

candidates.rationale: publish_node starts with a zero digest and only replaces it for a 64-byte string that successfully hex-decodes. Wrong length or invalid hex still reaches BftMessage::sign and send; the Python binding forwards the string without validation. source_checks.observation: Malformed text leaves payload_hash zero before unconditional signing and sending.
Sign/verify bind the digest actually supplied.
Binding forwards arbitrary hash text.

guards: Transport allocation/send errors still propagate.
The length condition protects copy_from_slice length for valid hex but does not reject malformed input.
No signature forgery is alleged; the publisher legitimately signs the wrong digest.

candidates.rationale: Every domain queue is deque(maxlen=capacity), and routing appends without a full-queue check while total_dispatched increases. Python bounded deques evict the oldest item on append. The pipeline dispatches the complete frame batch before draining domains, so more than capacity accepted frames for one domain silently remove earlier work.

source_checks.observation: Telemetry lacks overflow count; all queues have maxlen.
Validation and FFI checks precede unchecked queue append and success count.
Whole batch is dispatched before any domain drainage.

guards: MAC/channel identity, monotonic Lamport tick and FFI publish guards reject malformed/unpublished frames.
The finding requires valid frames that pass those guards and exceed per-domain capacity before drainage.
Corrupted-drop telemetry is updated on other failures but no queue-eviction counter exists.
